A woman in her 70s with a history of recurrent stasis dermatitis treated with long-term topical and systemic corticosteroids presented to the clinic with painful swelling over the right lower leg of 1 week's duration. Physical Examination:
There were necrotic ulcers covered by hemorrhagic crusts and purulent debris on the right lower leg. She was afebrile.
